  - Each case first shows the plant took:
    - A real `gitleaks dir` run on B alone, with the repository's `.gitleaks.toml`, must give exactly `["generic-api-key"]`. A alone must give nothing.
    - The base's one-per-file form is then the oracle: it must leave B out and keep A.
  - Each case then calls this worktree's `gov.secrets.indexable` twice in the box's empty `HOME`. `GOV_SECRETS_CACHE` names a reuse-record file under that `HOME`.
  - Both calls must leave every B out, keep every A, and equal the oracle's list in the order asked. No secret value may appear in `.gov-runtime`, `.git`, the process tmp, `HOME` or the streams.

- discoveries:
  - The box environment sets `GOV_SECRETS_CACHE=""`, which uses no cache at all. The reuse record is therefore off in the existing second-run case. My case names the cache file under `box.home/.cache/gov-os/` so the second call really goes through it.
  - At this head the bug shows only when A comes first. With B first, B is caught on its own and the verdict is right.
  - The failure message for the red cases names only paths, never values.
- risks:
  - The second-call assertion (the reuse record must not answer B clean) is never reached while the first call is red. It is untested until the fix lands, so the lead should run it once then.
  - I could not read `gov/secrets`, so I don't know the reuse-record file format or batch boundaries. The spread case is meant to cover batch boundaries without knowing them.
  - I did not assert that the cache file is written, because I can't see the implementation. If the fix writes its record elsewhere, the second call may exercise no reuse.
- lessons: the shadow only appears when the secret-bearing file comes second, so a pair test must cover both orders. A batch-boundary-independent spread case is cheaper than guessing the batch size.
